Abdul Malek, Senior Advocate, (Abdur Rezzaque Khan, Additional Attorney-General, with him) instructed by B Hossain, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Rafique-ul Huq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Wahidullah, Advocates--on-Record—For the Respondent.

full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: This leave petition at the instance of the State has been preferred seeking leave to appeal against the order dated 24-3-2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2222 of 2004 granting ad-interim bail to the accused-respondent in Badda PS Case No. 6(9) 2003 dated 2-9-2003. 

 2. The facts disclosed in the leave petition are that one Shah Alam was killed on 1-9-2003 and the aforesaid case was started out of the occurrence on the basis of a First Information Report lodged by one Monirul Islam and that in the First Information Report the informant mentioned the names of two persons namely, Amir Hossain and Ripon as the accused but the name of the respondent was not mentioned therein though the First Information Report was lodged more than 12 (twelve) hours after the occurrence and the aforesaid two persons mentioned in the First Information Report being arrested were forwarded to the Court of learned Magistrate and they were released on bail and that on 7-9-2003 the informant filed a supplementary First Information Report stating, inter alia, that the deceased before his death named the respondent and some others as his assassins and prayed for inclusion of aforesaid name as accused in the First Information Report and the application has been forwarded to the investigating officer for taking steps and that though the supplementary First Information Report was lodged on 7-9-2003 but after about 6(six) months suddenly the police raided the residence of the respondent in the early hours of 21-3-2004 and the respondent No.1 has been shown arrested in connection with the said case and that he was then produced before the learned Magistrate on 21-3-2004 and an application for bail was filed and the learned Advocates of the respondent made their submissions in support of the prayer for bail and the State was also heard but the learned Magistrate fixed the matter on 28-3-2004 for further hearing and that on the same day another application was filed on behalf of the respondent praying to reconsider his prayer for bail and for allowing weekly bail reversing the earlier order passed for further hearing on 28-3-2004 and the learned Magistrate again rejected the said application. The respondent, therefore, filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 732 of 2004 before the learned Sessions Judge praying for bail and the learned Sessions Judge observing that the bail matter was pending before the Court below returned the case back to the learned Advocates for filing the same after disposal and did not thus entertain the prayer and that thereafter the respondent claiming to be an industrialist and owner of Daily Jugantor and Jamuna Television filed an application for bail before the High Court Division under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and their Lordships by order dated 24-3-2004 after hearing the learned Advocate of the respondent as well as the learned Deputy Attorney General and Mr Abdul Malek, learned Counsel, specially appointed by the Government, issued Rule in the matter returnable within 3(three) weeks fixing the matter for hearing on 17-4-2004 allowing ad-interim bail to the respondent for 4(four) months. Hence is this petition. 

 "The amount of every bond executed under this Chapter shall be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case, and shall not be excessive; and the High Court Division or Court of Sessions may, in any case, whether there be an appeal on conviction or not, direct that any person admitted to bail, or that the bail required by a police-officer or Magistrate be reduced." 

 11. On perusal of the aforesaid provision of law we are of the view that the Court of Sessions as well as the High Court Division have concurrent jurisdiction to entertain application for bail of an accused, moreso, if he is in custody. The High Court Division and the Court of Sessions though have concurrent jurisdiction under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is, however, correct to say that the practice in our High Court Division is that the Court of inferior jurisdiction is moved first. But in the instant case we have seen that the Court of Sessions was also moved without any success. The High Court Division and the Court of Sessions having concurrent power under the said section, we do not dispute that in the case of concurrent jurisdiction the lower court should be moved first but it is not an inviolable biblic rule. In exceptional circumstances the higher Court can also be moved. Section 498 of the Code speaking of the High Court Division or Court of Sessions, we do not find any reason to curtail the jurisdiction of the High Court Division and thus to negate the intention of the legislature making the superior Court subservient to the Court below. 

 12. After considering the facts and circumstances of the present case we do not find that the High Court Division had no jurisdiction to entertain the application. 

 "We have examined the order passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and it appears that the subsequent prayer made by the accused-petitioner for reconsidering the earlier order passed fixing the date on 28-3-2004 for bail was rejected and the order seemed to be a clear rejection of the grayer for bail, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, could have exercised his jurisdiction under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Having not done so this court can exercise its power under section 498 CrPC. Have heard Mr Abdul Malek and also the learned Deputy Attorney General the accused-petitioner Md Nurul Islam @ Babul is granted ad-interim bail in Badda PS Case No. 6(9) 2003 dated 2-9-2003 to the satisfaction of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for a period of 4(four) months from date.
